concepts.name: Abductive Reasoning
concepts.short_description: Inference to best explanation from incomplete data; hypothesis generation, explanatory virtues.

concepts.name: Epistemology
concepts.short_description: Study of knowledge, justification, and belief; foundationalism, coherentism, reliabilism.

concepts.name: Model Checking
concepts.short_description: Exhaustive verification of finite-state systems against specifications; temporal logic, state space exploration.

hypotheses.statement: Counterexample as surprise: the model checker's counterexample (or a world trace that contradicts the verified model) is the surprising fact that triggers abduction; the abduced object is a minimal model repair; a repair becomes knowledge only when it survives re-verification plus fresh traces. Experiment: repair loops on hidden automata, measuring trace-efficiency and brittleness of repairs.

Knowledge as a model-checkable modal property: the agent's epistemic state is a finite set of candidate models (epistemic alternatives); 'the agent knows phi' is literally 'phi holds in every remaining candidate', decided by model checking; abduction is the operator that removes and adds candidates. Experiment: track the frontier of known formulas as evidence accumulates and test for discontinuous jumps and false-knowledge events.

Explanatory virtue as verification cost: the virtue that abduction should maximize is not description length but the cost of exhaustively checking the explanation; cheap-to-verify explanations are preferred because only they can be justified by the agent's bounded checker. Experiment: pit a verification-cost prior against an MDL prior where the two disagree (short programs with huge reachable state spaces).

Three justification topologies as three state-space regimes: foundationalism = acyclic support graph with axioms, coherentism = greatest consistent fixed point of mutually constraining models, reliabilism = temporal property over the history of a belief-forming process. Experiment: insert abductive hypotheses into each topology and measure retraction avalanches and consistency maintenance cost.

Safety/liveness epistemic asymmetry: from finite evidence, safety claims are refutable but never finitely verified by traces alone, liveness claims are neither finitely refutable nor verifiable; abduction of a model is what lets an agent come to 'know' liveness, so liveness knowledge is structurally more abduction-dependent and more fragile. Experiment: compare false-knowledge rates for safety vs liveness formulas under matched base rates.

Spec-relevant abstraction as justified granularity: an agent that abduces an abstraction only as fine as a specification requires (CEGAR-style) holds beliefs at the coarsest granularity that justifies its decisions; distinctions the spec does not need are never believed. Experiment: compare spec-triggered splitting with prediction-error splitting and measure whether the learned partition aligns with the spec-relevant quotient.

Gettier cases as unrealized witnesses: a belief can be true and model-checked (justified) while its witness path does not exist in the real system; this is a checkable, mechanical definition of epistemic luck. Experiment: flag beliefs whose certificate path was never observed and test whether they fail more under mechanism shifts.

Counterexample-guided abductive repair: an agent holds a finite automaton model plus a fixed spec; whenever a world trace contradicts the model, it abduces the minimal edit (add state / redirect transition / flip label) that explains the trace AND keeps the spec satisfied; edits are provisional until they survive k fresh traces.

concept_contributions.Abductive Reasoning: generates minimal edits that explain the contradicting trace
concept_contributions.Epistemology: provisional vs accepted status of edits (defeasibility with a survival criterion)
concept_contributions.Model Checking: spec-preservation check on every candidate edit

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: no repair is proposed; the agent can only reject its model
knockouts.Epistemology: every edit is treated as final; no distinction between repaired and known structure
knockouts.Model Checking: edits are unconstrained; becomes ordinary passive automaton learning

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Passive state-merging automaton inference (RPNI-style) on the accumulated traces, ignoring the spec.

questions.what_exists: a hidden automaton, a spec it satisfies, a candidate model, traces
questions.what_is_selected: edits that both explain traces and keep the spec true
questions.what_can_reproduce: accepted edits are reused as templates for later repairs
questions.what_can_transfer: the repair operator to a new automaton family with the same spec
questions.distinguishing_observable: traces-to-identification is lower than spec-free inference when the spec is true, and HIGHER when the spec is subtly false

hypotheses.statement: Verification-cost prior: explanations are ranked by the number of reachable states the agent must explore to check them against its spec battery, not by description length; the agent prefers explanations it can afford to justify.

concept_contributions.Abductive Reasoning: the candidate explanation set to be ranked
concept_contributions.Epistemology: the norm that only checkable beliefs may be held (justification access)

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: nothing to rank; mechanism is a pure cost-of-verification metric
knockouts.Epistemology: cost preference loses its rationale and becomes an arbitrary speed prior
knockouts.Model Checking: falls back to description length; cost measure disappears

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Speed prior / Levin-style time-bounded simplicity, or plain MDL.

questions.what_exists: candidate explanations with description length and reachable-state count
questions.what_changes: the ranking as the spec battery grows
questions.what_persists: explanations with small reachable state spaces
questions.what_can_learn: which explanation family the world uses
questions.what_can_transfer: cost-ranking to a world with a different spec battery
questions.distinguishing_observable: in worlds where short descriptions have huge state spaces (e.g. large modular counters), cost-prior picks different explanations than MDL and differs in held-out accuracy

hypotheses.statement: Epistemic frontier by exhaustive checking: the belief state is a finite set of candidate models; knowledge of phi is computed by model checking phi in every candidate; abduction adds candidates on surprise, evidence removes them; the agent acts only on known formulas.

concept_contributions.Abductive Reasoning: adds candidates when all current ones fail to explain an observation
concept_contributions.Epistemology: defines knowledge as truth in all epistemic alternatives
concept_contributions.Model Checking: decides phi in each candidate exhaustively

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: the candidate set can only shrink and may become empty (no recovery from a bad initial lot)
knockouts.Epistemology: the set is just a hypothesis pool with no knowledge operator; agent acts on majority not unanimity
knockouts.Model Checking: knowledge must be estimated by sampling; false-knowledge rate changes

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Version-space learning with a unanimity vote.

questions.what_exists: candidate models and a formula battery
questions.what_can_reproduce: candidates spawn repaired variants via abduction
questions.what_can_learn: which formulas are true of the world
questions.what_can_transfer: the frontier procedure to new formula batteries
questions.distinguishing_observable: the known-formula frontier grows in discrete jumps whose timing is predicted by candidate-set disagreement, and false-knowledge events occur only after abductive re-population

hypotheses.statement: Certificate-chained justification: each accepted belief stores the model-checking certificate (witness or invariant) that justified it and the abductions that model depended on; retracting an abduction recursively invalidates all beliefs whose certificates depended on it.

concept_contributions.Abductive Reasoning: the abductive hypotheses that can later be retracted
concept_contributions.Epistemology: foundationalist transmission of justification along support links
concept_contributions.Model Checking: the certificates themselves (witness paths, inductive invariants)

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: no retractable hypotheses: dependencies never change
knockouts.Epistemology: no transmission: beliefs are retracted one at a time without propagation
knockouts.Model Checking: no certificates: dependency links must be declared by hand (plain truth maintenance)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Justification-based truth maintenance system (JTMS). Likely a familiar mechanism in disguise.

questions.what_can_transfer: the dependency structure to new domains
questions.distinguishing_observable: retraction cascade size distribution vs a system without certificate links

hypotheses.statement: Coherence fixed point under abductive insertion: beliefs are mutually constraining small models; after each abductive insertion the checker recomputes the greatest mutually consistent subset; the system exhibits retraction avalanches whose size distribution depends on how tightly models constrain each other.

concept_contributions.Epistemology: coherentist global consistency as the maintained quantity
concept_contributions.Model Checking: fixed-point computation of the consistent subset

knockouts.Epistemology: no global coherence requirement; insertions never trigger retractions
knockouts.Model Checking: consistency is judged locally or heuristically; avalanches become arbitrary

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Incremental random constraint satisfaction with greedy conflict removal.

questions.what_exists: a web of small models linked by shared propositions
questions.what_can_learn: nothing learns; this is a law of the belief web
questions.distinguishing_observable: avalanche-size distribution shape (heavy-tailed near a density threshold vs exponential)

hypotheses.statement: Reliabilist process selection: a population of abductive procedures (minimal-edit, merge-states, most-recent-reuse, random-consistent) each proposes models; a procedure's weight is the fraction of its past proposals that later passed model checks on held-out traces; beliefs are held with the weight of the process that produced them, not the evidence for the belief.

concept_contributions.Epistemology: the reliabilist norm: justification is the reliability of the producing process
concept_contributions.Model Checking: the pass/fail oracle that builds each track record

knockouts.Epistemology: weights attach to hypotheses, not processes (ordinary Bayesian mixture)
knockouts.Model Checking: track records must come from noisy prediction scores

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Multiplicative-weights / Hedge over experts. Weak three-way dependency: epistemology relabels expert weighting.

questions.what_can_reproduce: not applicable unless procedures are mutated
questions.what_can_learn: which procedure fits the world family
questions.what_can_transfer: procedure weights across a family shift
questions.distinguishing_observable: after a world-family shift, process-level weighting and hypothesis-level weighting recover at different rates

hypotheses.statement: Spec abduction with asymmetric credence: the agent abduces temporal-logic properties of the world from finite traces; safety-type hypotheses are refutable by a finite trace, liveness-type are not; the agent assigns structurally lower ceiling credence to abduced liveness properties unless they are entailed by an abduced model.

concept_contributions.Abductive Reasoning: generates candidate properties to explain regularities and absences in traces
concept_contributions.Epistemology: credence ceilings tied to refutability class
concept_contributions.Model Checking: classification of properties as safety/liveness and checking them against candidate models

knockouts.Epistemology: all properties get the same credence rule; asymmetry disappears
knockouts.Model Checking: the safety/liveness distinction cannot be computed; credence rule is undefined

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Frequency-based confidence with a fixed discount for rarely observed events.

questions.what_can_transfer: credence rules to new property classes
questions.distinguishing_observable: false-knowledge rate for liveness vs safety at matched base rates and matched formula length

hypotheses.statement: Horizon-tagged belief: the checker runs with depth bound k; every belief carries its horizon tag and the agent must represent 'unknown beyond k' separately from 'true'; abduction is only allowed to fill in beyond-horizon structure when a spec forces it.

concept_contributions.Epistemology: the distinction between known-up-to-k and known

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: beyond-k is always unknown; agent never extrapolates
knockouts.Epistemology: horizon tags collapse; bounded truth is treated as truth

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Finite-horizon lookahead with a confidence decay.

questions.what_persists: beliefs verified at every horizon tried
questions.what_can_learn: where the world's behaviour changes beyond short horizons
questions.distinguishing_observable: error rate at horizon k+j as a function of j for tagged vs untagged agents in worlds with late-onset violations

hypotheses.statement: Spec-disagreement exploration: the agent chooses actions that maximize disagreement among candidate models about whether the SPEC holds (not about next-state predictions), so exploration concentrates where verification verdicts are uncertain.

concept_contributions.Abductive Reasoning: the candidate models whose disagreement defines the target
concept_contributions.Epistemology: the epistemic goal is knowing the spec's truth, not knowing the world

knockouts.Epistemology: goal reverts to model identification (next-state disagreement)
knockouts.Model Checking: disagreement must be computed on predictions

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Query-by-committee active learning on next-state predictions.

questions.what_changes: the candidate set via chosen experiments
questions.distinguishing_observable: fewer actions to decide the spec, but WORSE full-model identification than prediction-disagreement exploration

hypotheses.statement: Spec-driven abstraction growth: the agent starts with a one-state abstraction of the world and splits abstract states only when a counterexample to the spec turns out spurious on real traces; the belief partition therefore grows only as fine as the spec requires.

concept_contributions.Abductive Reasoning: the choice of which split explains the spuriousness
concept_contributions.Epistemology: the abstraction is the agent's justified granularity of belief
concept_contributions.Model Checking: abstract counterexample generation and spuriousness check

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: splits are chosen at random among states on the spurious path
knockouts.Epistemology: no rationale for stopping; granularity is set by budget
knockouts.Model Checking: no counterexamples; splits must be triggered by prediction error

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Decision-tree / state splitting driven by prediction error (U-tree-like).

questions.what_can_reproduce: partitions reused when the spec changes slightly
questions.what_can_learn: the spec-relevant quotient of the world
questions.what_can_transfer: abstraction to a new spec sharing propositions
questions.distinguishing_observable: the learned partition aligns with the spec-relevant quotient and ignores spec-irrelevant labels that prediction-error splitting captures

hypotheses.statement: Witness grounding (mechanical Gettier detection): a belief phi is flagged as lucky if it is true in the world and verified in the agent's model but its certificate (witness path) has never been realized in observed traces; lucky beliefs are held at reduced strength and prioritized for testing.

concept_contributions.Abductive Reasoning: the model in which the witness lives came from abduction and may contain fictitious structure
concept_contributions.Epistemology: the Gettier distinction: justification that does not connect to the truthmaker
concept_contributions.Model Checking: the witness path as an explicit certificate

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: models are learned only from observed structure; fictitious witnesses rarely arise
knockouts.Epistemology: no distinction between grounded and lucky truths
knockouts.Model Checking: no certificate to compare against observation

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Novelty/visit-count confidence: trust predictions on paths you have seen more.

questions.what_can_learn: which parts of the model are fictitious
questions.distinguishing_observable: after a mechanism shift, flagged-lucky beliefs fail at a higher rate than grounded ones matched for visit counts

hypotheses.statement: Bisimulation-quotient epistemics: hypotheses that are bisimilar with respect to observable labels are identified; abduction operates on quotient classes; the agent never distinguishes observationally equivalent explanations and cannot represent a preference between them.

concept_contributions.Epistemology: underdetermination made explicit: indistinguishable alternatives count as one epistemic state

knockouts.Epistemology: agent keeps separate beliefs about indistinguishable models (and may wrongly prefer one)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Minimal DFA / Myhill-Nerode minimization. Weak three-way dependency: epistemology only names the quotient.

questions.what_can_learn: the observational quotient of the world
questions.distinguishing_observable: sample efficiency gain equal to the average class size; if none, the quotient buys nothing

hypotheses.statement: Skeptic-believer game: a skeptic searches (by model checking over candidate structures) for a counter-model consistent with all evidence in which the believer's claim fails; the believer answers by abducing a discriminating experiment; a claim becomes knowledge when the skeptic's bounded search is exhausted.

concept_contributions.Epistemology: skeptical scenarios as the test of knowledge

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: believer cannot respond; skeptic always wins or the game is passive
knockouts.Epistemology: no role structure; reduces to consistency checking
knockouts.Model Checking: skeptic samples counter-models; exhaustion never certified

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Minimax active learning / version space with worst-case queries.

questions.what_persists: claims that survived exhaustive skeptic search
questions.what_is_selected: experiments that kill the most counter-models
questions.distinguishing_observable: claims certified by the game have lower false-knowledge rate than claims certified by unanimity of a randomly sampled candidate set of equal size

hypotheses.statement: Abductive directed mutation under a verifier guard: an evolving population of candidate automata mutates by abducing a minimal edit that fixes one misclassified example, and offspring that violate a known spec are killed before selection.

concept_contributions.Epistemology: defeasibility and a norm that no individual may hold a spec-violating belief

knockouts.Epistemology: guard is replaced by fitness penalty (beliefs allowed to violate norms)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Hill climbing with error-directed edits and a constraint penalty.

questions.what_exists: population of automata, labeled examples, spec
questions.what_is_selected: automata with best training accuracy among guarded
questions.what_can_transfer: the directed-mutation operator to other automaton families
questions.distinguishing_observable: a positive directed x guard interaction on generations-to-fit and held-out accuracy

hypotheses.statement: Obligation memory: memory stores open temporal obligations (pending 'until' and 'eventually' formulas implied by current beliefs) instead of facts; a belief is demoted when an obligation it created expires unmet and promoted when obligations are discharged.

concept_contributions.Epistemology: justification is earned by discharged obligations over time
concept_contributions.Model Checking: runtime monitor automata for the obligations

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: obligations arise only from given rules
knockouts.Epistemology: discharge does not change belief status

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Prediction-error tracking with delayed credit assignment.

questions.what_is_selected: beliefs whose obligations tend to be met
questions.distinguishing_observable: beliefs promoted by obligation discharge are more robust to later evidence than beliefs promoted by equal counts of immediate confirmations

hypotheses.statement: Loveliness as checkable scope: an explanation's loveliness is the number of spec formulas it makes decidable within the checker's budget; the agent prefers lovely explanations over merely likely ones and the question is whether loveliness predicts future survival beyond likelihood.

concept_contributions.Abductive Reasoning: the lovely/likely distinction in explanation choice
concept_contributions.Epistemology: explanatory virtue as a guide to truth (contested)

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: no alternative explanations to prefer among
knockouts.Epistemology: virtue has no claimed link to truth; preference is aesthetic

questions.what_persists: lovely explanations if loveliness tracks truth
questions.what_can_learn: whether loveliness is truth-conducive in a world family
questions.distinguishing_observable: partial correlation between loveliness and future survival controlling for likelihood and size

hypotheses.statement: Surprise tax: in a world where every unexplained observation costs the agent, and every model-checking step also costs, the agent must trade abductive repair against verification; the rule predicts an interior optimum of checking effort per repair that shifts with world stochasticity.

concept_contributions.Abductive Reasoning: repair as the response to surprise
concept_contributions.Epistemology: the rational allocation of justification effort

knockouts.Abductive Reasoning: no repair option; agent just pays surprise
knockouts.Epistemology: no normative target; optimum is just cost minimization

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Exploration-exploitation cost trade-off; bounded rationality with two costs.

questions.distinguishing_observable: optimum effort shifts non-monotonically with noise; a monotone shift indicates plain cost trade-off

hypotheses.statement: W4 probe round 1: SIGNAL. Outcome SIGNAL. Treatment: 1747 true verified beliefs (1252 lucky, 495 grounded); post-shift failure rate lucky 0.3769968051118211, grounded 0.2585858585858586; MH OR 1.5795840110000243, p 0.00017881593763680224. Null twin MH OR 0.998177526075097, p 1.0. Cheat OR inf. Positive control: 300/300 planted flagged, failure rate among flagged 1.0. Numbers only; no claim beyond this toy configuration.

lenses.name: Counterexample genealogy
lenses.rationale: Every accepted belief in this triplicate descends from a counterexample; the ancestry of repairs is where abduction and checking meet.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: log of (counterexample, abduced edit, verification outcome) events
lenses.transformation: build a DAG from each edit to the counterexample that triggered it and to earlier edits it modified
observables: fraction of final model edges with a live ancestor chain
predictedSignals: spec-guarded repair produces shallower, more reused genealogies
unguarded repair produces long chains of patches on patches
lenses.nullExpectation: genealogy depth distribution matches that of edits triggered by random misclassified examples
failureModes: genealogy dominated by trivial one-step repairs
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: structural history of the belief system, invisible in accuracy curves

lenses.name: Knows-frontier trace
lenses.rationale: Turns the epistemic operator into a time series: which formulas the agent knows at each step.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: candidate-model set over time and a fixed formula battery
lenses.transformation: at each step model-check every formula in every candidate; record unanimous-true, unanimous-false, split
observables: false-knowledge events (known-true but false in world)
predictedSignals: false-knowledge events cluster right after abductive re-population
lenses.nullExpectation: frontier grows smoothly and false-knowledge events are uniform in time
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: separates knowing from being accurate on average

lenses.name: Justification ledger thermodynamics
lenses.rationale: Checking has a cost in states explored; belief entropy has a cost in wrong actions; the ratio is the exchange rate of justification.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: per-step reachable-state counts and candidate-set entropy
lenses.transformation: compute bits of candidate-set entropy removed per 1000 states explored, per repair
predictedSignals: verification-cost prior achieves higher exchange rate early and lower late
lenses.nullExpectation: exchange rate equal across priors within seed variation
failureModes: state counts dominated by one pathological candidate
entropy estimates degenerate when the set is tiny
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: cost-side view absent from accuracy and frontier lenses

lenses.name: Retraction avalanche spectrum
lenses.rationale: Coherentist and foundationalist webs respond to insertions by retraction cascades; their size distribution is a fingerprint of topology.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: belief in/out status before and after each insertion
lenses.transformation: count beliefs flipped per insertion; fit exponential vs power-law tail by likelihood ratio
predictedSignals: heavy tail near a critical web density for coherence dynamics
short exponential tail for certificate-chained foundationalist webs
lenses.nullExpectation: exponential tail independent of web density
failureModes: finite-size cutoff mistaken for tail shape
insertion stream correlated with web structure
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: global dynamics of the belief web, not individual belief quality

lenses.name: Refutability-class split
lenses.rationale: The safety/liveness distinction divides beliefs into finitely refutable and not; this lens asks if the agent's errors respect that division.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: formula battery labeled safety / liveness / mixed, credence trajectories
lenses.transformation: stratify all epistemic metrics by refutability class at matched base rate and formula size
predictedSignals: liveness false-knowledge rate exceeds safety rate when knowledge comes via abduced models
lenses.nullExpectation: rates equal once base rate and length are matched
failureModes: class labels confounded with formula size
too few liveness formulas become known
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: shows whether a formal-methods distinction shapes epistemic error

lenses.name: Witness grounding audit
lenses.rationale: Gettier luck is checkable when justifications are explicit paths.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: agent's witness paths and the set of observed concrete traces
lenses.transformation: mark each true, verified belief as grounded (witness realized in traces) or lucky (not realized)
observables: post-shift failure rate of lucky vs grounded
predictedSignals: lucky beliefs fail more under mechanism shift even at matched visit counts
lenses.nullExpectation: failure rates equal once visit counts are matched
failureModes: lucky flag is just a proxy for low visit count
witness choice arbitrary among many witnesses
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: an explicit luck variable not present in any accuracy or frontier measure

lenses.name: Spec-relevance alignment map
lenses.rationale: Abstractions should carve the world where the spec needs it; this measures where the carving actually falls.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: learned partition of concrete states and two reference partitions (spec-relevant quotient, full observational quotient)
lenses.transformation: compute adjusted mutual information of the learned partition with each reference
predictedSignals: spec-driven splitting aligns with spec-relevant quotient and stays small
lenses.nullExpectation: alignment with both references proportional to partition size alone
failureModes: references nearly identical in the chosen worlds (no contrast)

experiments.hypothesis: Abstraction that is split only on spurious spec counterexamples aligns with the spec-relevant quotient of the world and stays smaller than prediction-error splitting with the same split budget.
experiments.mechanism: CEGAR-style loop: one-state abstraction; model-check safety spec AG not p_bad on abstraction; if counterexample, replay on concrete traces; if spurious, split the abstract state at the failure point on the concrete predicate that separates the replayed states.
experiments.control: Same splitting procedure but triggered by next-label prediction error (U-tree-like), same maximum number of splits.
experiments.positive_control: Planted world where p_bad depends only on a 2-state component product with a 20-state irrelevant component; spec-driven splitting must recover exactly the 2-block partition (AMI >= 0.95).
experiments.observable: AMI of learned partition with spec-relevant quotient (A_spec) and with full observational quotient (A_full); partition size.
experiments.success_criterion: Over 30 seeds, median(A_spec - A_full) for the treatment exceeds the same median for the control by >= 0.15 (Wilcoxon signed-rank p < 0.01), and median treatment partition size <= 0.6 x control.
experiments.failure_criterion: Difference < 0.05 or p > 0.1, or treatment partition size >= control size.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Any splitting procedure with fewer splits looks more spec-aligned because coarse partitions trivially match the coarse reference.
experiments.null_twin: Split times copied from the treatment run (matching split count and timing) but split location chosen uniformly among states on the replayed path: preserves split budget, destroys counterexample information.
experiments.why_this_implementation: Explicit finite labeled transition systems keep the spec-relevant quotient computable exactly; no learned function approximator is needed or wanted.
experiments.size: 40-state random LTS, 3 actions, 2 propositions (p_bad spec-relevant, q irrelevant), 200 random-walk traces of length 30, max 20 splits, 30 seeds
stupid_explanations: coarser partitions trivially score higher AMI with a coarse reference
the random LTS generator makes q correlated with p_bad
the spurious-check replays only a few traces so splits are effectively random

experiments.hypothesis: When knowledge is defined as truth in all remaining candidate models and candidates are refilled abductively, liveness formulas reach 'known' status with a higher false-knowledge rate than safety formulas of matched base rate and length.
experiments.mechanism: Candidate set of Kripke structures; finite trace prefixes eliminate candidates; when the set empties, abduce minimal repairs of the last surviving candidates; knowledge frontier computed by CTL model checking every formula in every candidate.
experiments.intervention: Evidence stream of finite prefixes; knowledge certified by unanimity over abductively maintained candidates.
experiments.control: Same stream, candidate set drawn fresh from the prior when it empties (no abductive repair).
experiments.positive_control: Candidate set containing the true structure and never emptying: false-knowledge rate must be 0 for both classes.
experiments.observable: False-knowledge rate FK_live and FK_safe = fraction of known formulas that are false in the true structure, per class.
experiments.success_criterion: Over 40 seeds, FK_live / FK_safe >= 2 with bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 1.2, and the ratio under the control is < 1.5.
experiments.failure_criterion: Ratio CI includes 1, or the control shows the same ratio (asymmetry not abduction-dependent).
experiments.alternative_explanation: Liveness formulas in the battery are simply harder or have different truth base rates.
experiments.null_twin: Randomly permute the safety/liveness labels across formulas matched on length and base rate: nuisance statistics identical, refutability class destroyed; ratio must go to ~1.
experiments.why_this_implementation: Exhaustive CTL checking over small explicit structures gives exact knowledge; a probabilistic learner would blur the unanimity definition that the mechanism depends on.
experiments.size: true structure 20 states, 500 candidates, 20 safety + 20 liveness formulas matched on length and base rate, prefixes up to length 30, 60 prefixes per run, 40 seeds
stupid_explanations: the random structure generator makes liveness formulas almost always true so any error looks large
few liveness formulas become known, so the ratio is noise
the repair operator systematically adds self-loops that satisfy AF-type formulas

experiments.hypothesis: Directed abductive mutation and a spec guard interact: the guard helps directed mutation more than it helps random mutation.
experiments.mechanism: Population of DFAs; directed mutation picks one misclassified string and applies the minimal edit (redirect one transition or flip one accept bit on its run) that fixes it; guard rejects offspring whose product with the spec's violation automaton is non-empty.
experiments.intervention: 2x2 design: mutation in {directed, random} x guard in {on, off}.
experiments.positive_control: Spec equal to the exact hidden language: guard alone must drive all guarded arms to 100% held-out accuracy.
experiments.observable: Generations to 100% training accuracy (capped), held-out accuracy on 1000 strings, final spec-satisfaction fraction; L1 genealogy depth.
experiments.success_criterion: Over 40 seeds per arm, the interaction coefficient in a linear model of log(generations) is negative with bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0, and held-out accuracy of directed+guard exceeds random+no-guard by >= 0.05.
experiments.failure_criterion: Interaction CI includes 0, or directed+guard held-out accuracy <= random+guard.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Directed mutation is simply a better local search and the guard is a generic regularizer; the interaction could be a ceiling effect.
experiments.null_twin: Directed mutation that targets a correctly classified string of the same length instead of a misclassified one: identical edit locality statistics, no counterexample information.
experiments.why_this_implementation: Explicit DFAs make the spec guard an exact emptiness check; an RL or neural policy would replace the guard with a penalty and destroy the norm-as-hard-constraint reading.
experiments.size: hidden 6-state DFA over {a,b}, candidate DFAs up to 10 states, population 50, 200 training strings length <= 12, 300 generations cap, 40 seeds x 4 arms
stupid_explanations: the spec eliminates most of the hypothesis space so guarded arms are just searching a tiny space
the cap on generations produces a ceiling-driven interaction
the hidden DFA family is so small that directed edits find it by enumeration

experiments.hypothesis: True, model-checked beliefs whose witness paths were never realized in observed traces (lucky beliefs) fail more often after a mechanism shift than grounded beliefs matched on visit counts.
experiments.mechanism: Agent learns a Kripke model from traces with abductive completion of unobserved transitions; for each reachability-type formula it records a witness path; witness grounding marks it grounded if the path appears in traces.
experiments.intervention: Mechanism shift: one of two redundant mechanisms (disjoint paths making EF goal true) is disabled at random.
experiments.control: Beliefs grouped by visit-count deciles of the states on their witness paths, ignoring grounding.
experiments.positive_control: Planted cases where the witness uses a fabricated transition and the disabled mechanism is the only real support: flagged beliefs must fail at rate >= 0.9.
experiments.observable: Post-shift failure rate of lucky vs grounded beliefs within visit-count decile strata.
experiments.success_criterion: Pooled over 60 seeds x 30 formulas, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel common odds ratio of failure (lucky vs grounded, stratified by visit decile) >= 1.5 with p < 0.01.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Lucky flag is a proxy for being far from the start state or for low visit counts.
experiments.null_twin: Flag a random subset of true verified beliefs as lucky at the same rate and with the same visit-count distribution: nuisance matched, grounding information destroyed.
experiments.why_this_implementation: Explicit witness paths exist only in an explicit-state model; a learned value function has no certificate to ground.
experiments.size: 16-state true structure with 2 redundant goal mechanisms, 80 training traces length 20, 30 reachability formulas, 60 seeds
stupid_explanations: lucky beliefs concentrate on the disabled mechanism by construction of the shift
witness selection picks shortest paths that happen to use abduced edges
visit-count strata too coarse to remove the confound

anomalies.text: post-run descriptive check (not part of outcome): in TREATMENT, fail == touches_disabled for all 1747 beliefs; a belief fails iff s or t is an interior state of the disabled mechanism. Beliefs with an endpoint in either mechanism interior: n=1093, lucky 0.772, fail 0.549; beliefs with no such endpoint: n=654, lucky 0.624, fail 0.000. The lucky-vs-grounded OR may be carried by endpoint location (stupid explanation 1), which visit strata do not remove.
1747/1800 formulas are true and verified (world is nearly strongly connected); 96% of lucky witnesses use a fabricated reverse edge, 0% of grounded ones.

rejected_explanations: visit-count strata too coarse to remove the confound
